# Workspace appearances

The palette button between Gmail status and the light/dark control offers
**Purple** and **Vercel**. Appearance and color mode are independent. Purple is
the default; the browser remembers an explicit choice. Both appearances retain
the compact Compose heading, recipient summaries, role badges, and checklist.
The Vercel appearance uses the approved Compose references in `../compose` and
keeps the subsequently approved bright-yellow personalization highlights.

## Scope and behavior

Compose, Templates, Contacts, History, Usage, Settings, and billing use the
selected appearance. Public pages and admin retain their own existing styling.
The saved color mode continues to apply as before on public pages.

`mailloop-appearance` stores `purple` or `vercel`; the existing `mailloop-theme`
key still stores `light` or `dark`. Preferences synchronize across tabs. Blocked
storage falls back to in-memory choices for the document. No account setting,
API, or database changes are required.

The root pre-paint script initializes both choices. A single root-mounted
runtime tracks the active route and updates `data-workspace`, `data-appearance`,
and `data-theme` on the document. This avoids stale styling from Next.js's
retained, hidden route trees. Workspace-only Vercel tokens also reach native
dialogs and portaled menus/tooltips.

Page-local colors and decorative effects have appearance-aware overrides;
Purple retains its existing values. Vercel uses neutral surfaces, 6–8px controls
and panels, solid contrasting buttons, blue focus and links, coral section
labels, restrained glow, and semantic status feedback. Recipient rows and
status pills keep their deliberately rounded shapes.

- [Chooser](screenshots/appearance-chooser.png) and [mobile chooser](screenshots/appearance-chooser-mobile.png)

- Mobile Vercel: [Contacts](screenshots/contacts-vercel-dark-mobile.png), [Usage](screenshots/usage-vercel-light-mobile.png)

## Verification

Typecheck, lint, formatting checks, and 12 unit tests passed. The unit tests
exercise pre-paint initialization for every combination, route scoping, defaults,
invalid storage values, blocked storage, preview substitutions, and send estimates.

All 36 targeted browser configurations have been verified across desktop and
mobile, including all four appearance/mode combinations on the six main workspace
routes. Accessibility scans and viewport overflow checks passed. Tests cover
keyboard selection and dismissal, independent preferences, reload persistence,
cross-tab updates, blocked writes, public-page isolation, recipient selection,
templates, attachments, individual campaign sends, and quota/Premium dialogs.

The mobile outside-click test was corrected to tap the page edge rather than a
heading underneath the open chooser; the corrected selector test passed on both
projects. The relevant commands are:

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm test -- tests/appearance.test.ts tests/redesign.test.ts
npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only '--browser=app.spec.ts,feature-gates.spec.ts,--grep,workspace appearance|compose theme|send-limit popup|send-limit boundary|individual campaign queue|attachment defaults|compose bulk selection'
npx tsx scripts/test-usage-db.ts --e2e-only '--browser=app.spec.ts,--grep,workspace appearance selector'
```

Work remains on `theme`, uncommitted and unpushed.
